Spell out every step, or sketch a few and see how it looks. You hold the gate.

Before saying done, it builds and renders every step — and fixes what breaks.

This presentation was built exactly this way. Thanks for watching.

criteria.rationale: The Talk boundary uses the kit correctly. The shared ReferenceScene mostly does too. But it bypasses and duplicates the kit's node mechanism for five entities. The tray, verify, socket and modify entities are raw `motion.div layout layoutId` elements. The conversation arrow is a hand-written `motion.svg layout layoutId` with its own arrow path. The kit already supplies these through `Node` (shared.tsx) and `Arrow`. `Node` adds the `LAYOUT_T` transition and `data-presentation-node`. `Arrow` adds the same arrow path. The raw elements skip both, so they re-implement the shared layout mechanism and lose the kit's transition timing.
evidence: Talk.tsx renders `<Presentation steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode="browse" />`, so orchestration goes through the kit.
ReferenceScene.tsx uses kit `SceneLayer`, `Box`, `Label`, `Frame`, `Emphasis` and `SymbolChip` for most entities.
ReferenceScene.tsx hand-rolls `motion.svg ... layoutId={E.conversation}`, with its own arrow path, instead of the kit `Arrow`.
ReferenceScene.tsx hand-rolls `motion.div layout layoutId={E.tray}`, `E.verify`, `E.socket` and `E.modify` instead of `Box`, `Frame` or `Label`.
shared.tsx `Node` applies `transition={{ duration: LAYOUT_T }}` and `data-presentation-node`; the raw elements apply neither.
judging basis: majority-fail

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping: steps/index.tsx builds all nine steps from one outline map, each with Scene: ReferenceScene and groupKey: 'reference-scene'. Stage calls sceneTransitionKey, which uses resolveGroup. That matches adjacent steps with the same groupKey and Scene and returns the same key, `group:reference-scene:0`, for all nine. The motion.div keyed on it therefore stays mounted and receives new payload props instead of remounting. Identity: entities.ts holds the presentation-owned ENTITIES ids. ReferenceScene passes them as id to Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis and SymbolChip, and as layoutId on raw motion elements. Node and SceneLayer forward the id to motion's layoutId with layout, so the same id in consecutive steps morphs in place. groupKey preserves the mount; layoutId preserves entity identity.

Stage.tsx: motion.div key={transitionKey} wraps <SceneComponent payload={step.payload} />
entities.ts ENTITIES; ReferenceScene uses E.you, E.prompt, E.skill, E.question, E.tray, the card ids, E.depth, E.socket, E.verify, E.modify, E.edited and E.reveal as id or layoutId
shared.tsx Node and SceneLayer.tsx: layout layoutId={id}
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: Unmet clause: for an empty or unscaffolded target, the fixture says the skill "performs a full scaffold ... and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation" and "SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed." The span quotes all of SKILL.md (lines 1-47). Line 26 directs the full scaffold by copying templates/bootstrap/. Line 32 only merges the required dependency names into package.json, and its one install command is `npx playwright install chromium`. Section 3 (line 38) then creates the presentation. Section 4 (line 44) runs `npm run build` straight away. No line anywhere in the file tells the agent to run `npm install`, `npm ci` or any equivalent for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide, ESLint or Playwright. The bootstrap package.json (lines 1-38) has no install or postinstall hook that would fill that gap. So the procedure declares the dependencies but never installs them, which means it assumes they are already present. This is Judge B's reason, and the full file confirms it. Judges A and C say SKILL.md directs dependency installation. Their evidence is the line 32 dependency list and the Chromium command. But listing package names to merge into package.json is not installing them, and installing Chromium only fetches a browser binary, not the npm packages. They also point to scripts/presentation-template.test.ts, which copies the bootstrap and runs `npm ci`. That is the test harness's own setup, not the skill's procedure, so it cannot meet the clause requiring the skill itself to install the dependencies. Their observations (template contents, the materialization test, kit alignment) are accurate, but they do not decide this clause.
evidence: skills/presentation/SKILL.md line 26: "For a full scaffold, copy `templates/bootstrap/` into the resolved app root." No install step follows it.

subcomponents.title: Verification tooling robustness

criteria.rationale: Every exit path in all six copies (repository and bootstrap template copies of verify.mjs, verify-presentation.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs) terminates the preview server and awaits its exit. Each script starts the server itself with `spawn(process.execPath, [<root>/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js, 'preview', ...])`. There is no npm or npx wrapper, so the child being killed is the preview server process. That spawn, the bounded readiness loop, `chromium.launch`, and every check sit inside one `try`. Its `finally` closes the browser and, if `preview.exitCode === null`, sends SIGTERM. It then awaits `Promise.race([new Promise(r => preview.once('exit', r)), delay(3000)])` and sends SIGKILL if the server is still running. The failing-check path also reaches that `finally`. In both verify copies, `fail` is defined as `function fail(phase, message) { throw new Error(...) }` (verify.mjs line 10, verify-presentation.mjs line 16). It throws and never calls process.exit, so readiness failure, readiness timeout and every failing render check unwind through the `finally`. The `.catch(() => fail(...))` calls on `waitForFunction` rethrow inside the awaited promise, so they propagate the same way. The top-level callers catch the error and set `process.exitCode = 1`, which also never calls process.exit, so cleanup finishes before the script exits. In inspect, every failure inside the try is a literal `throw`, and the catch sets `process.exitCode = 1` before the `finally` runs. The `process.exit` calls at inspect lines 20, 21 and 25 happen before the preview is spawned at line 45, so no preview exists yet on those paths. A browser launch failure (`chromium.launch` at verify.mjs:48, verify-presentation.mjs:57, inspect:64) happens after the spawn and inside the try, so it reaches the same cleanup. Success falls through to the `finally` as well. The bootstrap copies match the repository copies line for line. Judges A and B are consistent with this source. Judge C points to the SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupt handler, which calls process.exit(130) without awaiting the preview's exit. The criterion's guidance lists the exit paths to trace as success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and an error after the preview started; signal interruption is not among them, so it does not decide the requirement. Even on that path the handler sends SIGTERM to the vite server itself, not to a wrapper. Judge C's second point is that the SIGKILL fallback is not awaited. That does not decide the requirement either: the `finally` already awaits the server's 'exit' event after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL is only a last resort for a server that is still alive after the bounded wait.

criteria.rationale: No delivered automated test drives a browser directly. The vitest files are unit tests, file checks, and a materialization test that shells out to `npm run verify`. That script waits on state with waitForFunction on data-step-index, and none of the tests use sleeps or waitForTimeout. No test sleeps for a fixed time.
evidence: A search of all *.test.ts files finds no playwright, chromium, waitForTimeout or setTimeout usage.
presentation-template.test.ts drives the browser only through `npm run verify`, which polls with page.waitForFunction on step index.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The tests start no preview server or browser themselves. The only test that reaches a preview is the materialization test, which runs `npm run verify`. That script allocates a free port with listen(0) and runs vite directly with --strictPort. On every exit it kills the preview and awaits its exit. No test hardcodes a port or kills only an npm/npx wrapper.
evidence: presentation-template.test.ts: runs execFile('npm',['run','verify']) in a temp copy.
verify-presentation.mjs render(): `server.listen(0,'127.0.0.1')` port allocation; the finally block kills and awaits the vite child.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The round-0 log records real observations for most evolving-scene behaviors: nine-step order, keyboard, touch, direct jump, boundaries, mode toggle and position, attribution, and active-state hooks. The skill journeys (AT-001, AT-002, AT-004) are disclosed as an environmental impediment (I-1), so they do not count against coverage. Still, several scenarios the environment allowed were left unexercised by the candidate's own choice. The log gives 'additional variants were not needed' as the reason and records no environmental barrier. Unexercised: missing or malformed sample; console or page error fails verification; step error fails verification; seeded suspicious-overlap, intentional-overlap, indistinct-active-chrome and unpolished-attribution diagnostics; new-entity-enters-after-others-settle (not isolated); typed payloads (only a build result); unstyled kit output; and a full `npm run verify` run. Persisting-entity morph was checked only by DOM node identity, which is weaker than the motion scenario states. Together this leaves most of the visual-inspection-warning feature and most of the verification failure scenarios (3 of 4) unexercised. Later rounds only re-checked F-1 and found nothing new.
evidence: Round 0 log: 'Missing sample / browser runtime or console failure / failed transition: Not exercised; these require additional fault variants.'
Round 0 log: 'Seeded overlap/exemption, indistinct active chrome, attribution warning diagnostics: No seeded diagnostic fixtures were exercised.'
Round 0 log: 'New entity enters after persisting entities settle: Not isolated.'
Round 0 log: 'Persisting entity morphs / grouped scene update: ... retained the same DOM node' (DOM identity only).
Round 1 log: 'Newcomer timing..., full missing-sample/runtime-error/transition-failure matrix, and seeded visual-warning fixtures ... were not rerun.'
judging basis: majority-fail

criteria.rationale: The assumptions ledger's maintainability pass claims that `npm run verify` passed for all nine steps. It also claims `npm test` (38 pass), lint, and `sync:templates --check` all passed, and that `npm run inspect` captured 9 steps. These claims map to the basis scenarios "Build must succeed", "Every step renders cleanly", and "Checks run before done". The ledger attributes them to the implementation run. No command output or log for them is in the packet. The only logs present are two inspector/build logs from the tester's disposable copy. They show a build plus `inspect` PASS, not `verify`. The tester's own round-0 and round-1 inspect logs are also unresolved references, absent from the packet. The ledger's `npm run verify` result therefore has no backing artifact, and attributing it to the implementation run does not prove it.
evidence: The ledger states "Verification completed successfully: `npm run sync:templates -- --check`, `npm test` (9 files, 38 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run verify` (all nine steps)&qu…
The packet's logs contain only `tsc -b && vite build` and `[inspect] PASS: captured 9 steps`, with no `verify` output.
The findings index lists round1-narrow-inspect.log and round1-wide-inspect.log as unresolved references.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: The tested revision is recorded as 935ebfe, which is the final revision. The harness shows zero product, test-only and harness changes between the tested revision and final. The earlier pass at eea1152 also shows an empty change set to its tested revision. No listed product file is unexplored.
evidence: The tested-revision artifact records 935ebfea13b00e3ca1ecfb631e415d8a7204dded.
Lineage shows final_sha equals the tested sha, with zero product changes.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The record discloses what it did not exercise: the skill journeys (I-1), unisolated newcomer timing, unrun fault variants, and not running full verify or tests under the acceptance skill. It also discloses the unconfirmed /tmp profile cleanup (I-2), the absence of hosted CI, the draft-PR CodeRabbit skip, and the unresolved U-items. It reports NOT_READY and does not overclaim. It states that the DOM-persistence and opacity observations are weaker than full motion sequencing. The F-1 revision history is transparent. The disclosed differences about narrow readability (small but readable, with a residual threshold question) do not show any claim to be false.
evidence: The handoff reports "Result: NOT_READY due I-1 and I-2" and the CI absence.
The exploration log's "Deliberately not exercised" section.
The findings history records the F-1 reevaluations and the carried I-1/I-2.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The record surfaces every requirement deviation it observed. The narrow-viewport unreadable text (F-1) was reproduced and recorded as a finding, then fixed and re-verified. The ghost-card exit gap and the favicon-filter gap were recorded and fixed. Spec gaps that couldn't be resolved are logged as decisions: the ToC breakpoint (U1), MIN_SCALE (U2), the narrow readability threshold (U3), the card count (U4) and the verify scope (U5). The unexercised skill journeys (I-1) and the /tmp profile cleanup (I-2) are recorded as impediments. I found no observed deviation that goes unmentioned.
evidence: Ledger rows 1-7 and U1-U5 give each unresolved item a 'Why undecided' note, a decision question and options.
Findings F-1, I-1 and I-2 are recorded in the findings history with evidence paths.
The exploration log lists what was deliberately not exercised (public skill journeys, newcomer-timing isolation, seeded diagnostics).
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The record separates what it measured from what it infers. It states plainly that the spec gives no numeric values for the ToC breakpoint, MIN_SCALE or a readable text size. It does not call the reproduced narrow-readability violation acceptable: it fixed it, re-measured 12.03px rendered height, and kept the residual threshold question open as U3. It also says what it did not verify, such as the ghost fade not being captured by eye and the skill journeys not being exercised. One small inconsistency: the ledger says text renders at about 8-10px while the tester measured 12px. That does not misstate the requirement or a repository fact.
evidence: U1/U2 say the spec 'never gives a width' and 'gives no value'.
F-1 was reproduced (3-5px text), fixed, and re-measured at 12.03px; U3 stays open.
'Not checked by eye. I did not capture the 0.35s ghost fade itself'.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The workflow fixed on its own authority only the items the approved requirements already settle: the ghost-card exit under the 'Departing entity exits' scenario, and the favicon filter. It escalated the product and design choices the spec leaves open (breakpoint, MIN_SCALE, readability threshold, card count, verify scope). It declined to add new skill policy (a 24px guidance line) and a new inspector warning category, and said these are scope decisions. It escalated I-1 as not fixable by code, and offered options including accepting the limitation with its consequence stated. No reproduced violation was labelled optional.
evidence: The ledger fixes #3 and #6 and leaves U1-U5 for the user.
'I did not add that guidance because it is new skill policy.'
I-1 gives two options with consequences: run AT-001/002/004 in human acceptance, or accept the untested coverage.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The final handoff names I-1 and I-2 with their subjects and consequences. For the open product decisions it says only 'prior U1–U5 entries remain in the assumptions ledger.' That gives identifiers and a pointer but no subject for any of them. The reader isn't told that U1 is the ToC breakpoint, U2 MIN_SCALE, U3 narrow-viewport readability, U4 the step-card count, or U5 the verify scope. Nor does it say that U3's residual readability threshold is still undecided. Under the standard, a pointer to the ledger without naming the decisions fails. The handoff also states 'no new product ambiguity found' without preserving what remains open.
evidence: Handoff: 'Assumptions: no new product ambiguity found; prior U1–U5 entries remain in the assumptions ledger.'
The handoff does not describe the subject of U1, U2, U3, U4 or U5.
judging basis: consensus-fail

checks.rationale: The dissent argues for a pass, so it would have to answer the majority's reason: the shared ReferenceScene bypasses and duplicates the kit's node mechanism. It doesn't. It admits the raw `motion.div`/`motion.svg` elements exist and only argues they share the kit's LayoutGroup. The material shows the majority's point holds. The kit's `Node` in shared.tsx is `motion.div layout layoutId={id} transition={{ duration: LAYOUT_T }} data-presentation-node`, and it accepts any children, className and style. `Box` wraps `Node`. ReferenceScene doesn't use them for four plain containers: tray, verify, socket and modify. Each of these hand-writes `<motion.div layout layoutId={E.x} ...>`. That re-creates the layout/layoutId mechanism outside the kit and drops the kit's `LAYOUT_T` transition and `data-presentation-node` marker. Sharing Stage's LayoutGroup doesn't change that: these four entities still bypass the reusable Node/Box API and duplicate its behavior. The conversation arrow may be a harder case, since the kit's Arrow has a fixed one-way path. Even so, the four container bypasses alone leave the 'without bypassing or duplicating' requirement unmet at the shared Scene boundary. The dissent's correct points about Talk → Presentation → Stage don't cure that.

votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of the port with fetch, not from the child's own announcement. The only ownership check is preview.exitCode sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before the request. The port is reserved by listening and closing, so another listener could bind it before the child starts. That listener could answer a fetch before the child's exit is observed. Readiness is not raced against the child's exit event. This is the pattern the guidance says to fail.

Details by template: (1) Talk.tsx imports '../../presentation-kit/Presentation', which is src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx from src/presentations/<slug>/. It passes the required props steps and title, plus initialMode, all declared on PresentationProps in types.ts. (2) steps/step-01.tsx imports '../../../presentation-kit/types', which resolves to src/presentation-kit/types.ts from src/presentations/<slug>/steps/. Its Step literal uses id, era, title, caption, Scene and payload, which match StepMeta & { Scene, payload, groupKey? }. (3) steps/REPLACE_SCENE_NAME.tsx imports '../../../presentation-kit/nodes' and '../../../presentation-kit/types', and '../entities' resolves to the slug's entities.ts. SceneLayer, Box and Label each get the required 'id' (and children for SceneLayer). Their prop types are HTMLMotionProps-based, so the 'style' prop is valid. The component signature ({ step }: SceneProps) matches Scene<undefined>. (4) steps/index.ts imports './step-01' and exports a readonly tuple, which is assignable to readonly Step<T>[]. (5) entities.ts has no imports. (6) The inspect template (bootstrap scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs) imports './inspection-diagnostics.mjs' and './sample-outline.mjs'. Both exist in the bootstrap scripts directory and export every symbol the inspect template imports: overlapArea, isOverlapAllowed, stylesDistinct, attributionIssues, previewReadinessFailure and validateRegistration. The nodes index re-exports Box, Label and SceneLayer. The bootstrap tsconfig.app.json includes only 'src', so the .mjs scripts are not type-checked. The bootstrap's own starter presentation uses the same import shapes, and the test builds, lints and verifies a copy of the bootstrap.

presentation-skill.rationale: Most of this pass is supported. SKILL.md directs a full scaffold from `templates/bootstrap/`. It lists the full dependency set and gives an explicit `npx playwright install chromium` step, which counts as an install. votes.rationale: The primitives are typed from the element's props (HTMLMotionProps<'div'>), and Box strips its kit-only `Icon`. lines.text: Inspect the current project before writing. Detect three anchors by their contracts, not byte equality or cosmetic filenames:
1. Build setup: Vite + React + TypeScript and a working `npm run build`.
2. Scene kit: typed `Step`/`Scene` contract, stage/host, present/browse navigation, chrome, and fit-scale canvas.
3. Presentation index: a registry mapping slugs to presentation routes.

If already inside a presentation app, use it and preserve every present anchor. Otherwise, an empty or standalone project targets its root. Detect a monorepo from `workspaces` in `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or a `packages/` or `apps/` layout; target a self-contained app under `presentations/`. For a non-empty project missing the scene kit or index, state the target and wait for confirmation before writing.
For a full scaffold, copy `templates/bootstrap/` into the resolved app root. For partial scaffolding, copy only the missing contract area and its required dependencies:
- Missing build setup: merge the bootstrap's Vite, TypeScript, ESLint, HTML, and ignore configuration, plus `src/main.tsx` and `src/index.css`, into the app. Keep unrelated host files intact.
- Missing scene kit: copy `templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/` into the app's source tree.

- Missing presentation index/routing: merge the bootstrap's `src/presentations/index.ts`, `src/main.tsx`, and `src/Landing.tsx`, adapting imports/routes to existing host conventions while preserving registered entries.

Merge dependencies into an existing `package.json` by adding only missing required names and scripts; preserve existing values, scripts, package manager, workspaces, and unrelated dependencies. The full dependency set is runtime `react`, `react-dom`, `motion`, `lucide-react`; dev `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `typescript`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `@types/node`, `@eslint/js`, `eslint`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, `eslint-plugin-react-refresh`, `globals`, `typescript-eslint`, and `playwright`. Install Chromium with Playwright (`npx playwright install chromium`) for render verification. Do not add Tailwind or another framework unless the host already uses it or the user requests it.

The kit and host scaffold are style-neutral: no default palette, typography, borders, shadows, card/button appearance, spacing scale, or theme tokens. Visual styling belongs to the presentation or host.

Run `npm run build`, then at least a first-step browser render check with no runtime or console errors. Prefer the project-local `npm run inspect -- <slug>`; it captures settled screenshots and reports advisory diagnostics. Review the first and last steps plus every dense/key step. If responsive-sensitive, also inspect a narrow viewport, for example `npm run inspect -- <slug> --viewport=390x844`. Confirm the diagram fits its fixed canvas and does not collide with captions, ToC, progress, or controls. Review every warning: fix accidental overlaps, indistinct active chrome, and unpolished attribution in presentation-owned CSS; use the allow-overlap marker only for intentional readable overlaps. If no local inspection helper exists, put any temporary Playwright helper under the project root.

Fix failures and re-check. A lighter initial loop of build plus one-route render is acceptable while iterating; before reporting success, run the full `npm run verify` (build and all-step render checks). Never report success on failing output, and report any remaining advisories accurately.

first_results.rationale: All six scripts start the preview the same way: the repository's verify.mjs, verify-presentation.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, plus their copies in the skill's bootstrap template. Each runs `spawn(process.execPath, [node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js, 'preview', ...])`, so the child process is the Vite server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. The spawn, the readiness wait, `chromium.launch` and every check all sit inside one `try`. Its `finally` closes the browser. If the preview is still running, it sends SIGTERM, waits for the preview's 'exit' event (up to 3 seconds), and sends SIGKILL if the process is still alive. Success, a failing check (`fail()` throws), a browser launch failure and any error after the preview started all pass through that `finally`. The bootstrap copies have the same lines at the same line numbers. I agree with Judges A and B. Judge C's first reason is the SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupt handler, which calls `process.exit(130)` without waiting for the preview to exit. Neither the requirement nor its guidance names a signal interrupt as an exit path; they name success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after start. Judge C's second reason is that the SIGKILL fallback is not awaited. That fallback runs only after the awaited SIGTERM wait times out, and SIGKILL cannot be caught or ignored, so the server process itself is still terminated. Neither reason shows a named exit path leaving the preview running.

first_results.rationale: `renderSample` in scripts/verify.mjs reads the rendered page at every step. It opens `/${slug}` on the production preview and requires `data-step-count` to equal `referenceOutline.length`. At each step it requires `data-step-index` to equal the expected step. It then reads the visible `[data-presentation-title]` text and the `[data-presentation-caption]` innerText and compares them with `referenceOutline[currentStep]`, before pressing ArrowRight and waiting for the index to advance. That covers titles, captions and outline order. Registration is also checked on the page: an unregistered route would not render the sample chrome with nine matching steps. The fail clause is regular expressions matched over source text, and no sample check does that. `validateSample` uses plain `outline.indexOf` substring search. `validateRegistration` walks a TypeScript syntax tree; its only regex strips quotes from a property name. Judges A and C fail the criterion because these source-side checks exist. But neither check is a regular-expression match over source text, and the rendered-page checks they say are missing are present for every item. Their reason therefore does not trigger the fail clause. Judge B's reading matches the source.

results.rationale: Every exit path in all six copies (repository and bootstrap template copies of verify.mjs, verify-presentation.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs) terminates the preview server and awaits its exit. Each script starts the server itself with `spawn(process.execPath, [<root>/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js, 'preview', ...])`. There is no npm or npx wrapper, so the child being killed is the preview server process. That spawn, the bounded readiness loop, `chromium.launch`, and every check sit inside one `try`. Its `finally` closes the browser and, if `preview.exitCode === null`, sends SIGTERM. It then awaits `Promise.race([new Promise(r => preview.once('exit', r)), delay(3000)])` and sends SIGKILL if the server is still running. The failing-check path also reaches that `finally`. In both verify copies, `fail` is defined as `function fail(phase, message) { throw new Error(...) }` (verify.mjs line 10, verify-presentation.mjs line 16). It throws and never calls process.exit, so readiness failure, readiness timeout and every failing render check unwind through the `finally`. The `.catch(() => fail(...))` calls on `waitForFunction` rethrow inside the awaited promise, so they propagate the same way. The top-level callers catch the error and set `process.exitCode = 1`, which also never calls process.exit, so cleanup finishes before the script exits. In inspect, every failure inside the try is a literal `throw`, and the catch sets `process.exitCode = 1` before the `finally` runs. The `process.exit` calls at inspect lines 20, 21 and 25 happen before the preview is spawned at line 45, so no preview exists yet on those paths. A browser launch failure (`chromium.launch` at verify.mjs:48, verify-presentation.mjs:57, inspect:64) happens after the spawn and inside the try, so it reaches the same cleanup. Success falls through to the `finally` as well. The bootstrap copies match the repository copies line for line. Judges A and B are consistent with this source. Judge C points to the SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupt handler, which calls process.exit(130) without awaiting the preview's exit. The criterion's guidance lists the exit paths to trace as success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and an error after the preview started; signal interruption is not among them, so it does not decide the requirement. Even on that path the handler sends SIGTERM to the vite server itself, not to a wrapper. Judge C's second point is that the SIGKILL fallback is not awaited. That does not decide the requirement either: the `finally` already awaits the server's 'exit' event after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL is only a last resort for a server that is still alive after the bounded wait.

results.rationale: `renderSample` in scripts/verify.mjs reads the rendered page at every step. It opens `/${slug}` on the production preview and requires `data-step-count` to equal `referenceOutline.length`. At each step it requires `data-step-index` to equal the expected step. It then reads the visible `[data-presentation-title]` text and the `[data-presentation-caption]` innerText and compares them with `referenceOutline[currentStep]`, before pressing ArrowRight and waiting for the index to advance. That covers titles, captions and outline order. Registration is also checked on the page: an unregistered route would not render the sample chrome with nine matching steps. The fail clause is regular expressions matched over source text, and no sample check does that. `validateSample` uses plain `outline.indexOf` substring search. `validateRegistration` walks a TypeScript syntax tree; its only regex strips quotes from a property name. Judges A and C fail the criterion because these source-side checks exist. But neither check is a regular-expression match over source text, and the rendered-page checks they say are missing are present for every item. Their reason therefore does not trigger the fail clause. Judge B's reading matches the source.

audit_results.rationale: All six scripts are quoted in full: verify.mjs, verify-presentation.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, each in the repository and in the bootstrap template. Each script starts the preview by running process.execPath on node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js with 'preview'. The child process it later kills is therefore the Vite preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In every script, that spawn, the bounded readiness loop, chromium.launch and all the checks sit inside a single try. Its finally closes the browser. Then, if preview.exitCode === null, it sends SIGTERM, waits for the preview's 'exit' event (raced against a 3-second delay), and sends SIGKILL if the server is still running.
